study type: Cross-sectional analysis of a prospective cohort
exposure: human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) in breast milk
cohort: 157 Hispanic mother-infant pairs at 1 month, and 69 pairs at 6 months
finding: Several human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) were found to be both positively and negatively associated with infant food responsiveness.
mod_finding: Delivery mode was adjusted for as a potential confounder in the analysis of the association between human milk oligosaccharides and infant eating behaviour, but the study did not examine mode of delivery as a primary variable.
